title: SASSA Decline Reason: 'Income Source Detected' — What It Means & How to Fix
description: The most common SRD decline reason. SASSA found deposits in your bank account exceeding R624 for the month. Learn exactly what triggers this and how to appeal.
decline_code: Income Source Detected / Means Test Failed
what_it_means: SASSA's automated system scanned your bank accounts and found total deposits exceeding R624 for the month. The system does not distinguish between salary, gifts, stokvel payouts, family transfers, refunds, or any other type of deposit — any money coming in counts as income. This is one of the most common SRD decline reasons. The exact number of affected applicants is not published by SASSA.
common_triggers: A family member sent you money via e-wallet or bank transfer
A stokvel payout was deposited into your account
You received a UIF payment or NSFAS stipend
Someone used your bank account for their transactions
You do informal work that pays irregularly into your account

how_to_fix.detail: Review your bank statements for the declined month. Identify every deposit, including gifts, family transfers, and stokvel payouts.
Go to srd-appeals.dsd.gov.za and select the declined month. Choose 'Income Source Detected' as the reason. Explain what each deposit was — be specific about dates and amounts.
Upload bank statements showing the deposits. If a family member sent you money, include a signed affidavit explaining it was a gift, not income.
Use a separate bank account for SRD only, or have family give you cash instead of electronic transfers.

appeal_deadline: 90 days from the date of decline
success_rate: Appeals are most likely to succeed when the deposit was genuinely not income (family gift, stokvel payout, refund). Be honest and specific in your explanation and provide bank statements.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Decline Reason: 'Identity Verification Failed' — What It Means & How to Fix
description: Your name or ID number does not match Department of Home Affairs records. Learn why this happens and how to correct it step by step.
what_it_means: SASSA compared the personal details you submitted (name, surname, ID number) against the Department of Home Affairs database and found a mismatch. This is a security measure to prevent identity fraud. The mismatch could be caused by a simple typo, a name change after marriage, or an error in Home Affairs records.
common_triggers: A typo in your name or surname during application
You used a nickname instead of your full legal name
Your surname changed after marriage but was not updated at Home Affairs
Home Affairs has incorrect records for your ID number
Your ID document was recently issued and has not synced to all databases

how_to_fix.step: Check your name on the SRD portal
how_to_fix.detail: Log into srd.sassa.gov.za and verify that your name and surname are spelled exactly as on your ID document. A single letter difference can cause this decline.
Use the 'Request Names and Surname Update' tool on the SRD website if the spelling is wrong.
If you received an SMS with a facial recognition link, complete it within 72 hours.
If your ID records at Home Affairs are incorrect (e.g., listed as deceased, wrong surname), visit a Home Affairs office in person to correct the error.

appeal_deadline: 90 days from the date of decline
success_rate: Outcomes depend on the cause. A simple typo or name mismatch can usually be corrected by updating your details and reapplying. Corrections to Home Affairs records can take longer.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Decline Reason: 'UIF Registered' — What It Means & How to Fix
description: SASSA found that you are registered with the Unemployment Insurance Fund. Learn why this blocks your SRD grant and how to resolve it.
what_it_means: SASSA's system cross-checks your ID number against the Department of Employment and Labour's UIF database. If you appear as an active UIF contributor or recipient, your SRD application is declined. This happens even if you are not currently receiving UIF payments — simply being registered on the UIF system can trigger the decline.
common_triggers: Your previous employer did not deregister you from UIF when you left
You applied for and received UIF payments during the SRD assessment period
Your employer is still contributing to UIF on your behalf without your knowledge
There is an old UIF claim on your ID number from a previous job

how_to_fix.detail: Contact the Department of Employment and Labour to check if your UIF record is still active. You can visit your nearest Labour Centre.
Ask your previous employer to deregister you from UIF. If they refuse or cannot be contacted, the Labour Centre can assist.
Submit an appeal on the ITSAA portal. Include a letter from the Labour Centre confirming you are not receiving UIF benefits.

appeal_deadline: 90 days from the date of decline
success_rate: Provide a UIF deregistration letter or confirmation that you are not currently receiving UIF payments.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Decline Reason: 'NSFAS Registered' — What It Means & How to Fix
description: SASSA found that you are registered with NSFAS for student funding. Learn how to prove you are no longer a student and get your SRD grant approved.
what_it_means: SASSA checks your ID number against the National Student Financial Aid Scheme (NSFAS) database. If you appear as an active NSFAS beneficiary, your SRD application is declined. This often happens to students who graduated or dropped out but were never removed from the NSFAS system.
common_triggers: You graduated but the university did not update your status with NSFAS
You dropped out of your studies but NSFAS still shows you as active
You applied for NSFAS but never received funding
There is a data error linking your ID number to another student's NSFAS record

how_to_fix.step: Contact your university's financial aid office
how_to_fix.detail: Request a formal clearance letter confirming you are no longer registered as a student or receiving NSFAS funding.
On the ITSAA portal, upload your NSFAS clearance letter or proof that you are not currently funded.
Explain clearly: 'I graduated in [year] and am no longer a student. I am not receiving any NSFAS funding.'

appeal_deadline: 90 days from the date of decline
success_rate: Provide a clearance letter from the university financial aid office confirming your status.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Decline Reason: 'Existing SASSA Grant' — What It Means & How to Resolve
description: You cannot receive the SRD grant if you are already receiving another SASSA grant. Learn about the one-grant rule and what to do.
what_it_means: SASSA's system shows that you are already receiving another social grant — such as Old Age Pension, Disability Grant, Child Support Grant, Foster Child Grant, or Care Dependency Grant. South African law does not allow you to receive more than one SASSA grant at the same time (with limited exceptions for foster parents).
common_triggers: You are already receiving the Old Age Pension or Disability Grant
You are the primary caregiver receiving the Child Support Grant
Someone applied for a grant using your ID number without your knowledge
There is a data error linking your ID to another person's grant

how_to_fix.step: Check which grant you are receiving
how_to_fix.detail: Call the SASSA helpline at 0800 60 10 11 and ask which grant is linked to your ID number.
If you are receiving a permanent grant (R2,400 for Old Age/Disability), it pays much more than the SRD (R370) — you are better off with the permanent grant.
If someone else used your ID to apply for a grant, report it to the SASSA fraud hotline immediately.

appeal_deadline: No appeal needed — this decline is usually correct. Apply for the correct grant type instead.
success_rate: This decline is usually accurate. Only appeal if you believe a grant is fraudulently linked to your ID.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Decline Reason: 'Government Payroll Registered' — What It Means & How to Fix
description: SASSA found your ID number on a government payroll. Learn why this happens and how to prove you are no longer employed by the state.
what_it_means: SASSA cross-checks your ID number against the Government Employees Pension Fund and government payroll databases. If your ID appears on any government payroll system — even if you left years ago — your SRD application will be declined.
common_triggers: You previously worked for a government department and were never removed from the payroll
You were employed as a temporary educator, police reservist, or municipal worker
You are a former SANDF member with an active pension record
Your ID number was incorrectly linked to a government employee

how_to_fix.detail: Ask the government department you worked for to provide written confirmation that you are no longer employed.
Submit your appeal with the confirmation letter. Explain that you are no longer a government employee.
If the issue is with the pension fund, contact GEPF to confirm you are not receiving a government pension.

appeal_deadline: 90 days from the date of decline
success_rate: Provide a formal letter from the government department confirming you are no longer employed.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Decline Reason: 'Age Outside Range' — What It Means & Which Grant to Apply For
description: Your age does not meet the SRD grant requirement of 18–59. Learn which grant you qualify for based on your age.
what_it_means: The SRD grant is only available to applicants aged 18 to 59 (inclusive). If you are under 18 or over 59, your application will be declined with this reason. This is a hard requirement with no exceptions.
common_triggers: You are under 18 — the SRD grant requires applicants to be 18 or older
You are 60 or older — you qualify for the Old Age Grant instead
Your date of birth was entered incorrectly on the application form

how_to_fix.detail: You cannot receive the SRD grant. However, a parent or guardian may qualify for the Child Support Grant on your behalf.
Apply for the Old Age Grant (R2,400/month) at your nearest SASSA office. It pays much more than the SRD.

how_to_fix.step: If your age is incorrect on the application
how_to_fix.detail: The SRD portal does not allow you to change your date of birth. You must appeal explaining the error and provide your ID document as proof.

appeal_deadline: 90 days from the date of decline
success_rate: Appeal if your date of birth was entered incorrectly. If you genuinely do not meet the age requirement, apply for the correct grant type instead.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Decline Reason: 'Deceased Record on DHA' — What to Do
description: SASSA's system shows you as deceased according to Home Affairs records. Learn how to correct this serious data error.
what_it_means: When SASSA checks your ID number with the Department of Home Affairs, their database shows your ID as belonging to a deceased person. This is a serious data error — either Home Affairs has incorrect records, or someone fraudulently reported you as deceased.
common_triggers: Home Affairs has a data error linking your ID number to a deceased person
A family member mistakenly reported you as deceased (common with estranged families)
Identity theft — someone used your ID to fraudulently claim benefits and reported you as deceased to cover their tracks

how_to_fix.step: Visit your nearest Home Affairs office
how_to_fix.detail: This cannot be resolved online. You must go to a Home Affairs office in person with your ID document.
Ask Home Affairs to verify that you are alive and correct the database error.
Obtain a signed letter from Home Affairs confirming you are alive and the deceased record was an error.
Take the Home Affairs letter to your nearest SASSA office along with a new SRD application.

appeal_deadline: 90 days from the date of decline
success_rate: Appeal after the Home Affairs record is corrected. Expect delays — this process can take 2 to 4 weeks.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Decline Reason: 'Bank Details Invalid' — What It Means & How to Fix
description: SASSA declined your application because your banking details could not be verified. Learn how to update and verify your bank account so your grant is not blocked.
what_it_means: SASSA could not verify the bank account details you provided during your application or payment setup. This is not an eligibility decline — it means the payment cannot be processed until your banking information is correct and verifiable. The account holder name must match your ID, the account must be active, and the details must be in the correct format.
common_triggers: The account holder name you entered does not match your ID document
The bank account is closed, frozen, or deactivated
You entered an incorrect account number or branch code
The account is not linked to your ID number
You used a business or third-party account for your grant

how_to_fix.detail: Go to srd.sassa.gov.za and log in with your ID number and registered phone number.
Enter your full bank name, account number, branch code, and holder name exactly as on your ID.
Use a bank account registered in your own name, linked to your ID. Third-party or business accounts cannot be used.
After submitting, verification usually takes 3 to 7 working days. Check your status after that.

appeal_deadline: 90 days from the date of decline
success_rate: Fix your banking details on the SRD portal and verification is usually completed within a week. This is one of the easiest declines to resolve.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Decline Reason: 'Self-Correction Required' — What It Means & How to Fix
description: SASSA needs you to correct your own details after missing a biometric or verification step. Learn how to complete self-correction and avoid a decline.
what_it_means: SASSA requires you to complete a self-correction step — usually a biometric (facial recognition) verification or an update to your personal details — before your grant can continue. This status appears when you were flagged for enhanced security checks or when your details need to be confirmed by you. If you do not complete the self-correction within the given window, your status may move to 'Declined.'
common_triggers: You missed a biometric verification SMS link and did not complete it in time
Your identity could not be verified automatically and needs your confirmation
You were asked to correct a name or surname mismatch
You need to submit updated residence or bank information

how_to_fix.step: Check your SMS for a link
how_to_fix.detail: SASSA typically sends a biometric verification link by SMS. Open it within the validity window (often 72 hours).
Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the facial recognition process using your phone.
Use the 'Request Names and Surname Update' tool or update your residence information if asked.

how_to_fix.step: Check your status after completing it
how_to_fix.detail: Once the self-correction is complete, your status should update within a few days.

appeal_deadline: 90 days from the date of decline
success_rate: Self-correction is usually successful if you complete the biometric or detail update quickly. If you miss the window, appeal and explain what happened.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Decline Reason: 'Duplicate Application' — What It Means & How to Fix
description: SASSA found more than one application linked to your ID number. Learn why duplicates happen and how to get the correct one processed.
what_it_means: SASSA's system found more than one active or recent application linked to your ID number. This causes a decline because the system cannot determine which application is valid. Duplicates usually happen when you reapply before the previous application was closed, or when a family member or a copy of your ID was used to apply again. You only need one application on file.
common_triggers: You submitted more than one application in a short period
You reapplied while an earlier application was still in the system
Someone else used your ID number to apply for a grant
A data error created a duplicate record

how_to_fix.detail: Submitting additional applications will only create more duplicates. Stop applying and let one process.
Call the SASSA helpline on 0800 60 10 11 and ask them to identify and remove the duplicate application.
If the decline persists, lodge an appeal on the ITSAA portal explaining that only one application is valid.

appeal_deadline: 90 days from the date of decline
success_rate: Duplicates can usually be resolved by contacting SASSA to keep only one application. Fraudulent duplicates should be reported.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Decline Reason: 'Income Not Proven' — What It Means & How to Fix
description: SASSA could not confirm your income status. Learn why this happens and how to provide proof so your grant is not declined.
what_it_means: SASSA could not verify or confirm your income situation, so it could not establish that you meet the income threshold requirement. This is different from a decline because you have income — it means SASSA could not confirm that you have no income or income below the limit. You may need to provide proof so your application can be assessed.
common_triggers: Your banking information could not be fully checked
You did not provide complete income information on your application
There was a mismatch in the financial data SASSA could access
You have not received any income that SASSA could detect, leaving your situation unverified

how_to_fix.detail: Make sure your application states your income situation clearly and accurately.
Appeal on the ITSAA portal and explain your income situation, providing bank statements if helpful.
Ensure SASSA can access your bank accounts so it can verify your income level.

appeal_deadline: 90 days from the date of decline
success_rate: Appeals succeed when you can clearly demonstrate that your income is below the threshold and provide supporting evidence.
author: Lucky Cungwa
